clue.text: All for the vigorous and efficient making money

parts.note: to be all for something is to be in favour of it, pro
vigorous means fit, in good shape
efficient means able, capable

explanation.surface: A tribute to energetic, capable people who earn well.
explanation.definitionFit: A business making money is lucrative, turning a profit.

clue.text: A bird's fleece!

definitions.meaning: a crow-like bird that nests in colonies
to fleece is to swindle or cheat

explanation.surface: An exclamation about a bird's woolly coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fleece' suggests a woolly coat, but it is the verb meaning to cheat; the 's is a link meaning is.
explanation.definitionFit: The black corvid shares its name with a verb meaning to cheat someone out of money.

clue.text: Note: showed signs of injury made much of in story

parts.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
bled, as a wound does

explanation.surface: A memo that someone visibly hurt was exaggerated in the telling.
explanation.definitionFit: Something celebrated in legend, much told of in tales, is legendary.

clue.text: A manual worker filled up with divine fish

indicators.note: filled up with means the worker has the other piece placed inside

parts.note: a tiler works with the hands laying tiles
a divine is a theologian, a DD, Doctor of Divinity

explanation.surface: A labourer stuffed himself with heavenly fish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'divine' looks like an adjective, but it is a theologian, abbreviated DD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiny fish such as a minnow is a little catch, especially for children.

clue.text: Scrap about a badger

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the scrap goes round the other letter

parts.note: a scrap is a small bit

explanation.surface: A fight concerning an animal of the woodlands.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scrap' looks like a fight and 'badger' like an animal, but they are a piece and the verb to pester.
explanation.definitionFit: To badger someone is to torment or harass, as one might tease a creature.

clue.text: O ! model to thy inward greatness."Shakespeare (King Henry V)

definitions.text: O ! model to thy inward greatness."Shakespeare (King Henry V)

parts.words: O ! model to thy inward greatness."Shakespeare (King Henry V)
parts.note: fill the gap in this line from the Chorus of Henry V, which addresses the nation itself

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare's history play with its key word missing.
explanation.walkthrough: The Chorus before Act II of Henry V says the line; the missing word is the realm being addressed.
explanation.definitionFit: The Chorus apostrophises the kingdom of Henry V, the nation he rules.

clue.text: Businessman set against a player losing his head

parts.note: contra is Latin for against

indicators.note: losing his head means the first letter is dropped from the word for a player

parts.note: an actor is a player on stage

explanation.surface: A businessman is pitted against a performer who is losing his composure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing his head' suggests panic, but it drops the A from ACTOR to leave CTOR.
explanation.definitionFit: A builder or supplier who works under contract is a type of businessman.

clue.text: The woman who's got on board

definitions.text: The woman who's got on board

parts.words: The woman who's got on board
parts.note: a woman who sits on a company board, a female member of management

explanation.surface: A woman has embarked on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'got on board' suggests boarding a ship, but it means joining a company's board.
explanation.definitionFit: A female director of a company or institution sits on its board.

clue.text: A waste of big potential-there's nothing in that

indicators.note: there's nothing in that: the nought is placed inside the reshaped letters
potential means something not yet in its final form, so the letters of big are to be reshaped

parts.note: nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: A dismissive remark that a large prospect is empty of substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'potential' rearranges BIG to GBI, and 'in' puts O inside it after the G. The Gobi is the desert of Mongolia and China.
explanation.definitionFit: A desert is a waste, a barren tract of land; the Gobi is a famous one.

clue.text: The aim of lots is to be disagreeable

definitions.text: The aim of lots is to be
definitions.meaning: lots at an auction are put up to receive bids
disagreeable here means grim, off-putting, unwelcoming

explanation.surface: A gloomy saying that the purpose of many people is to be unpleasant.
explanation.walkthrough: The first reading splits the answer into two words, FOR BIDDING, which is what auction lots are offered for.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction lot is offered for bids; a stern, off-putting manner is grim and unwelcoming.

clue.text: See articles to shudder at

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
a is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Advice to look at some writings that will make you shudder.
explanation.definitionFit: To shudder at something is to detest it, feeling strong revulsion.

clue.text: Petty rogue taking a bow?

definitions.meaning: a violinist takes up a bow to play

explanation.surface: A small-time crook accepting applause on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking a bow' suggests a performer acknowledging applause, but it means picking up a violin bow.
explanation.definitionFit: A small-time swindler fiddles the books; a violin player draws a bow across the strings.

clue.text: Maybe fed after going around the church, improbable as it appears

indicators.note: going around means the rearranged letters surround the other piece
maybe signals that the following letters may be arranged another way

parts.note: CH is short for church

explanation.surface: Perhaps someone was fed after a trip round the church, unlikely as that seems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maybe' rearranges FED AFTER to FARFETED, and 'going around' puts it round CH.
explanation.definitionFit: An unlikely story is stretched beyond belief, hard to credit.

clue.text: Harmonious converse

parts.note: the opposite of in tune, as converse can mean the reverse

explanation.surface: Pleasant, agreeable conversation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converse' looks like a verb or noun for talk, but it means opposite.
explanation.definitionFit: The opposite of being in tune is jarring, clashing, out of tune.

clue.text: Concerned with holding out find a way

indicators.note: holding means containing, so the first piece wraps round the second

parts.note: re means concerning, about

explanation.surface: Worried about holding out, someone looks for a path.
explanation.definitionFit: A path or course to a destination is a way.

clue.text: Isn't worried by a worker for the moment

indicators.note: worried means pulled about, so the letters of the word isn't are shaken up

parts.note: an ant is the classic worker insect

explanation.surface: Someone stays calm for now despite a labourer's presence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worried' rearranges ISNT to INST.
explanation.definitionFit: An instant is a moment, a very brief point in time.

clue.text: Do some engraving, in the main terribly badly

indicators.note: in means the letters sit inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: A complaint that the engraving done is mostly awful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'engraving' is read as en-graving, putting into a grave; the letters straddle m-AIN TER-ribly.
explanation.definitionFit: To bury a body is to place it in a grave, so putting someone in a grave.

clue.text: Plump for a French male being included in the staff

indicators.note: being included in means placed inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a staff is a stick or rod
un is the masculine form of a in French

explanation.surface: A Frenchman joins the workforce and makes his choice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plump for' suggests choosing, but 'Plump' alone is an adjective meaning chubby; 'staff' is a stick, not employees.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump and its synonym both describe a pleasantly chubby, rounded figure.

clue.text: The others are idle

definitions.meaning: to be idle is to relax, take a break

explanation.surface: A complaint that everyone else is lazing about.
explanation.definitionFit: The remainder of a group are the others; to relax and do nothing is to be idle.

clue.text: A good man with the old complaint!

parts.note: ST, saint, is a good man
ye is an old form of the

explanation.surface: A virtuous man arrives with an old grievance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'complaint' suggests a grievance, but it means an ailment, a swelling on the eyelid.
explanation.definitionFit: A complaint here is a minor ailment, an inflamed swelling on the eyelid.

clue.text: To back a woman as the only alternative

indicators.note: to back here means to go backwards, so the word to is read in reverse

parts.note: her is a pronoun for a woman

explanation.surface: Someone supports a woman because she is the only option left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like support but turns TO into OT.
explanation.definitionFit: The other option is the remaining alternative when there are only two.

clue.text: Pilot through episcopal responsibility

parts.note: through can mean finished, over
a bishop's see is the diocese he is responsible for

explanation.surface: Guiding someone through a bishop's duties.
explanation.definitionFit: To pilot a project is to supervise and direct it.

clue.text: Communists set about the sailor making checks

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the communists surround the sailor

parts.note: reds are communists
a tar is a sailor

explanation.surface: Communists attack a sailor, carrying out inspections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set about' looks like attack but means surrounding.
explanation.definitionFit: To check progress is to slow or hinder it, delay it.

clue.text: The egghead got up about four, and that's wearing

parts.note: the head of egg is its first letter, E

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: got up means rose
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: An intellectual rose before dawn, and found it tiring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egghead' looks like an intellectual but gives the head of 'egg'; 'wearing' is not clothing but wearing away.
explanation.definitionFit: Something erosive wears things down, so it is wearing in the sense of abrading.

clue.text: Looks for an expression of goodwill

definitions.meaning: a greeting sent at the end of a letter, best wishes

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a friendly greeting.
explanation.definitionFit: To look at something is to gaze at it; best wishes sent in a letter are a goodwill greeting.

clue.text: Notorious gunmen turning to harangue following

indicators.note: turning means the gunmen's abbreviation is read backwards

parts.note: RA, the Royal Artillery, are gunners
to rant is to harangue

explanation.surface: Notorious gunmen turn to lecturing those following them.
explanation.definitionFit: Arrant means utter, out-and-out, as in a notorious villain.

clue.text: A guy scrounging a note in prison, right?

indicators.note: in means placed inside, so the note sits within the prison

parts.note: a cage is a place of confinement
D is a musical note

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man begging a bank note in jail is correct.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who scrounges is a sponger who begs or borrows without return.

clue.text: Discontinue work under way

indicators.note: in a down clue, under means the work comes below the way

parts.note: ST is short for street, a way
op, opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Halt the job that is in progress.
explanation.definitionFit: To discontinue something is to halt or cease it.

clue.text: A store where oil's available

indicators.note: available, with letters free to be used in any order, signals rearrangement

explanation.surface: A shop where oil can be bought.
explanation.walkthrough: 'available' rearranges OILS.
explanation.definitionFit: A tower or pit for keeping grain or fodder is a farm store.

clue.text: Dreadful Australian orgies

indicators.note: dreadful means in a terrible state, so the letters of the word are scrambled

explanation.surface: A disapproving remark about wild parties down under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dreadful' rearranges AUSTRALIAN, using every letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman winter festival was famous for revelry, so the word means wild parties.

clue.text: She's always seen in bed-naturally

indicators.note: the name is always visible within the run of letters, a sign to look inside

explanation.surface: A woman is naturally always found in bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The name sits across the hyphen: b-EDNA-turally.
explanation.definitionFit: A woman's name stands for she, a female person.

clue.text: Commentary is out of place

parts.note: ex is Latin for out of, as in ex-directory
a place is a position

explanation.surface: A remark that a piece of commentary is in the wrong spot.
explanation.definitionFit: An exposition is an explanatory account or commentary on a subject.
